_schema: THE ONLY place a sourced ticker, expense ratio or return may live. `funds` is keyed one entry per TICKER (upper-case); `vehicles` is keyed `provider::fund` in lower-case slugs, for a collective trust, separate account or guaranteed option that HAS no ticker. Every figure carries its as-of date and its source URL; er and ytd are percents as numbers (0.04 = 0.04%, -3.2 = -3.2%). A vehicle's `erBasis` says whose price it is -- `vehicle-stated` is the provider's published figure and is commonly NOT what a given plan pays, so it must never be printed as the plan's. Written by the fund-facts agent or by scripts/fund-facts-ingest.mjs from a provider capture in data/sources/; validated by node scripts/fund-facts-check.mjs, which runs in site-test. Nothing from memory, nothing undated, nothing unsourced. TRAILING RETURNS (opened 2026-11-06 for the owner's return curve): `r1y`, `r3y`, `r5y`, `r10y`, each with its own `<f>AsOf` and `<f>Source`. THEY ARE ANNUALISED, and an entry carrying any of them MUST declare `returnBasis: "annualised"` -- a 10-year CUMULATIVE return is about 2.6x its annualised one (10%/yr is +159% over a decade), so the two must never be interchanged, and the per-horizon plausibility bands are set to catch exactly that paste. Optional `inception` lets the checker refuse a 10-year figure on a fund that has not lived ten years. Providers quote every horizon at one month-end, so two different as-of dates in one entry warns: a curve drawn across them is not one quote. scripts/fund-facts-returns-test.mjs asserts each of these refusals in CI.
